questions.description: The only lamp nobody has to switch off at night.
questions.question: What gives us light and warmth during the day?
hints: It's a star.
We can't see it at night.
It's why we wear sunglasses and sunscreen.
questions.fun_fact: More than a million planets the size of Earth would fit inside the Sun.

questions.description: A planet that never leaves the house without its jewellery.
questions.question: Look at the picture: which planet is this?
hints: It's a gas giant.
It's the sixth planet from the Sun.
Its rings are made of ice and rock.
questions.fun_fact: Saturn is so light for its size that it would float in a giant bathtub full of water.

questions.description: A planet that went rusty because nobody dried it after the rain.
questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
hints: It's our neighbour.
Several robot rovers drive around on it.
It's named after the Roman god of war.
questions.fun_fact: Mars has Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the solar system.

questions.description: A big family that keeps walking around the same stove.
questions.question: How many planets are there in the solar system?
hints: Pluto doesn't count any more.
Four are rocky and four are giants.
It's the number of legs a spider has.
questions.fun_fact: The four planets closest to the Sun are rocky; the four farthest away are giants of gas and ice.

questions.description: The big brother who got the biggest bedroom.
questions.question: What is the largest planet in the solar system?
hints: It's a gas giant.
It's the fifth planet from the Sun.
It has a huge red spot that is a storm.
questions.fun_fact: More than a thousand Earths would fit inside Jupiter.

questions.description: Footprints nobody has swept away in more than fifty years.
questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
hints: He was American.
He flew on the Apollo 11 mission.
He said: "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind."
questions.fun_fact: Astronauts' footprints can last millions of years on the Moon, because there is no wind to blow them away.

questions.description: The one who sat so close to the fireplace that its toes went numb.
questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
hints: It's the smallest planet.
It has no moons at all.
It's named after the swift messenger of the Roman gods.
questions.fun_fact: A year on Mercury lasts only 88 Earth days.

questions.description: A trip around the world without a single stopover.
questions.question: Who was the first person to travel into space?
hints: It happened in 1961.
He was Soviet.
His spacecraft was called Vostok 1.
questions.fun_fact: Gagarin's flight lasted about 108 minutes: a single trip around the Earth.

questions.description: A sauna so extreme it melts lead.
questions.question: What is the hottest planet in the solar system?
hints: It's not the closest to the Sun.
Its thick clouds trap the heat like a greenhouse.
It's called the morning star.
questions.fun_fact: On Venus a day is longer than a year: it takes longer to spin once than to go around the Sun.

questions.description: The fastest messenger in the universe, and still it's late.
questions.question: How long does sunlight take to reach the Earth?
hints: Light travels about 300,000 kilometres per second.
The Sun is about 150 million kilometres away.
Long enough to boil an egg, too short to watch a film.
questions.fun_fact: Moonlight, on the other hand, takes just over a second to reach us.

questions.description: A year when half of humanity sat glued to the TV watching grey dust.
questions.question: In which year did a human first set foot on the Moon?
hints: It was during the space race.
It was near the end of a decade.
The Woodstock festival took place the same year.
questions.fun_fact: Twelve people have walked on the Moon, all of them between 1969 and 1972.

questions.description: Kicked out of the group chat, and nobody told it.
questions.question: Since 2006, what do astronomers call Pluto?
hints: It still goes around the Sun.
It's round, but shares its orbit with many other bodies.
Ceres and Eris have the same label.
questions.fun_fact: Pluto is smaller than our Moon.

questions.description: A planet that lay down for a nap and never got up again.
questions.question: Which planet spins almost lying down, its axis tipped on its side?
hints: It's an ice giant.
It was the first planet discovered with a telescope.
It's the seventh planet from the Sun.
questions.fun_fact: William Herschel discovered Uranus in 1781 and wanted to name it after King George III.

questions.description: A spacecraft that popped out for bread in the seventies and is still on its way.
questions.question: Which spacecraft is the farthest human-made object from Earth?
hints: It was launched in 1977.
It flew past Jupiter and Saturn.
In 2012 it became the first spacecraft to reach interstellar space.
questions.fun_fact: Both Voyager spacecraft carry a golden record with sounds and greetings from Earth.

questions.description: A moon that thinks it's a planet.
questions.question: What is the largest moon in the solar system?
hints: It's bigger than the planet Mercury.
It orbits Jupiter.
In Greek myth he was the cupbearer of the gods.
questions.fun_fact: Galileo discovered it in 1610, along with three other moons of Jupiter.
